`677-704`: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ **Include CPU-only mode in the constraints cache key.** `_cpu_only()` changes the generated requirements, but `ensure_constraints()` hashes only `req_files`. Toggling `ROCKETRIDE_CPU_ONLY_DEPS` can therefore reuse stale CPU/GPU constraints and install the wrong dependency set. Include the normalized CPU-only state in the cache key and cover both mode transitions with a regression test.

In `@packages/server/engine-lib/rocketlib-python/lib/depends.py` around lines 677 - 704, The constraints cache key in ensure_constraints must incorporate the normalized state returned by _cpu_only(), since that state changes generated requirements. Update the hash inputs so CPU-only and GPU/default modes produce distinct cache entries, and add a regression test covering both transitions to ensure stale constraints are not reused. ```
--- `691-704`: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ **Make CPU PyTorch resolution exclusive.** The new `--extra-index-url` directive still competes with PyPI because `_install_dry_run()` uses `unsafe-best-match`. A regular CUDA `torch` candidate can therefore win and reintroduce `nvidia-*` packages. Use an index strategy or explicit package-to-index directives that force PyTorch packages to the CPU index, then verify clean resolutions in both modes.

📒 Files selected for processing (1) * `packages/server/engine-lib/rocketlib-python/lib/depends.py`

Thanks @kwit75 — clear diagnosis (6.6 GB of never-executed CUDA traced to PyPI's default CUDA `torch` wheel), and the opt-in-not-auto-detected choice is right: with the flag unset the resolve is byte-identical to before, so self-hosted GPU users stay untouched. Re-reviewed at head `ae0b3f0`; the branch has not moved since my last pass.

**Request changes**

Both findings are in this body, not inline: the mechanism sits on unchanged lines (`_compute_hash` / `ensure_constraints`), and the one changed line that carries it (704) already has a CodeRabbit comment.

1. **MUST fix — the flag can silently no-op (blocking).** `_compute_hash()` (line 652) hashes only each requirement file's path, size and mtime; `ensure_constraints()` (lines 773-778) keys its "Constraints are up to date" early return on that hash alone, and `_cpu_only()` is not in the key. On any host that already built `constraints.txt`, setting `ROCKETRIDE_CPU_ONLY_DEPS` leaves the hash unchanged, so the rebuild is skipped, `_combine_requirements()` never re-runs, and the `--extra-index-url .../cpu` line is never emitted — the resolve goes green while still producing the CUDA set. Once CPU constraints are cached, unsetting the flag does not restore GPU either. Separately, `_write_excludes_file()` is rewritten every call and *does* honour the flag, so the excludes file can say `onnxruntime-gpu` while the stale `constraints.txt` still pins the CUDA `torch` — the two disagree. Fix: fold the normalized `_cpu_only()` into the cache key (seed `_compute_hash`, or add it to the stored-hash comparison). This is CodeRabbit's Major, confirmed at head: https://github.com/rocketride-org/rocketride-server/pull/1708#discussion_r3667439309 — their thread auto-marked "Addressed in commit ae0b3f0", but the code at that commit does not seed the key, so that marker is a false positive.

2. **should fix — no test covers the added behavior.** There is no pytest harness for `rocketlib-python` (zero Python test files, no test config, and `depends.py` imports `engLib` at module top on line 52, so it will not import outside `engine.exe`), so by our no-harness rule a missing test does not block this PR. But please make the new logic testable: make the `from engLib import ...` import lazy, or split `_cpu_only` / `_combine_requirements` / `_write_excludes_file` into an `engLib`-free module, then add a `test_depends.py` covering (a) the `--extra-index-url .../cpu` line appears only when the flag is set, (b) the excludes file flips `onnxruntime` <-> `onnxruntime-gpu`, and (c) the GPU->CPU / CPU->GPU cache-key transition from point 1. The missing engine-python test runner is worth a separate repo issue.

CodeRabbit's other Major — the unsafe-best-match index strategy (https://github.com/rocketride-org/rocketride-server/pull/1708#discussion_r3667439318) — does not block: your compile evidence (13 -> 0 `nvidia-*`) plus `+cpu` local-version priority make the CPU wheel win, and the strategy is unchanged. Its Darwin `onnxruntime-gpu` docstring Minor (https://github.com/rocketride-org/rocketride-server/pull/1708#discussion_r3669070099) is optional.
